method: Downloaded 25 exact images referenced by designated Notion paragraphs to internal research/figures and directly viewed each image with view_image. No pixel assets adopted into production.
rightsUsage: research-reference-only; no production asset authorization inferred

findings.observed: Phong drawing uses surface-to-light l, surface-to-viewer v, mirror direction r and theta between r/v; reflection construction is r=2(n·l)n−l. Blinn drawing uses h between v/l and theta between n/h.
findings.retainedRole: Same labeled vectors in our model; never reverse l accidentally; do not imply Phong and Blinn exponents produce identical widths.

findings.observed: 4×6 same-head grid varies highlight width and intensity independently; narrow bright highlights near right, intensity larger toward bottom.
findings.retainedRole: Use same owned object/light/camera with separate exponent and specular-color controls, not different models.

findings.observed: Rough-microfacet scatter sketch is conceptual, not Lambert proof. Incidence diagram compares perpendicular/glancing beams, fewer incoming rays per fixed surface length at grazing angle.
findings.retainedRole: Keep surface-projected-area explanation of n·l. No claim all roughness is diffuse or Lambert varies with outgoing viewing angle.

findings.observed: Four heads isolate specular + diffuse + ambient = lit; emission absent in this pictured example.
findings.retainedRole: Independently recreate component isolation; don't infer emission is included in source pictured sum.

findings.observed: Same teapot silhouette/geometry. Flat facets show hard lighting steps, Gouraud interpolates colors with less faithful interior highlight, Phong has smoother per-pixel highlight; silhouette remains polygonal.
findings.retainedRole: Same geometry and camera for all three; distinguish Phong interpolation from Phong specular model; show difference in shading, not subdivision.

findings.observed: Point example has a spherical cutoff-radius editor gizmo; spotlight shows apex position, inner hotspot cone, outer falloff cone and axial distance.
findings.retainedRole: Finite effect cutoff is renderer model, not physical point-source size; separate angular cone falloff and distance attenuation.

findings.observed: Plot compares inverse-square 100/d² with piecewise plateau/linear falloff dmin=10,dmax=60. Not equal curves; no finite cutoff for ideal inverse square.
findings.retainedRole: Our different small numbers still illustrate same functions with explicit units/illustration labels.

findings.observed: Omni projects circular center-bright 2D gobo, multiplied by 1D strip black→white→black; bounding geometry is box, lit room has soft pools on several surfaces.
findings.retainedRole: Demonstrate 2D gobo × 1D t attenuation inside volume. Axis-aligned box is computational influence region, not a physically spherical point light or fog volume.

findings.observed: Spot uses same circular 2D gobo; 1D strip is bright near left and dark at right; volume shown is frustum/pyramid-like widening projection, with a cone-like illumination patch on wall.
findings.retainedRole: Projective u/v division versus one-dimensional depth falloff; source marked 'box' filename must not cause geometry to be drawn as equal-sided cube.

findings.observed: Fake spot gets cone-like projected appearance from a triangular/teardrop 2D gobo with bright tip; 1D strip black→white→black; bounding volume remains a box.
findings.retainedRole: Explicit fake-spot illustration versus actual projective spot. Same general 2D×1D mechanism, altered maps/volume; no internal claim about modern commercial examples.

remaining: Unity outputs and footage integration require their own runtime/visual QA; these checks validate teaching roles only.
